title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 243
text:
6. The law gives a very specific definition of what it means to lack capacity for the purposes of
the Mental Capacity Act (MCA) 2005. It is a legal test, and not a medical test, and is set
down in s.2(1) MCA 2005, which provides that: “a person lacks capacity in relation to a
matter if at the material time he is unable to make a decision for himself in relation to the
matter because of an impairment of, or a disturbance in, the functioning of the mind or the
brain”.177

7. To apply the test, it can best be broken down into three questions:
• Is the person able to make a decision?
If they cannot:
• Is there an impairment or disturbance in the functioning of the person’s mind or brain?

177 Referred to as the “core determinative provision” in A Local Authority v JB [2021] UKSC52, paragraph 65.
Capacity (mental)

If so:
• Is the person’s inability to make the decision because of the identified impairment or
disturbance?178
